explanation: LocalDate.plusMonths adds the months and, if the resulting day-of-month does not exist in the target month, uses the last valid day of that month. February 2024 has 29 days because 2024 is a leap year, so 31 January plus one month is 29 February.

options.explanation: The day-of-month 31 is invalid in February, so the last valid day is used. 2024 is a leap year, which makes it the 29th.
This is what overflowing by days would give, but java.time never rolls over into the next month when adding months.
This would be correct in a non-leap year. 2024 is a leap year, so February has 29 days.
An invalid day-of-month after plusMonths is adjusted, not rejected. Exceptions come from invalid inputs to factory methods such as LocalDate.of.
